extracted.intended_audience: BBC content producers, editors, commissioning editors and independent production companies (with Programme Legal Advice and Editorial Policy stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial rules and mandatory referral triggers for gathering and broadcasting material that may infringe individual privacy, aimed at BBC programme-makers, editors and independent production companies. Covers high-level principles, how to assess legitimate expectation of privacy, data-handling, and specific situations requiring mandatory referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage justification for privacy infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: An infringement of privacy is considered in two stages, requiring justification for both the gathering and the broadcasting of material where there is a legitimate expectation of privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the act of obtaining material and the decision to broadcast it must be separately warranted; see Section 1 The BBC's Editorial Standards: 1.3 and Ofcom Broadcasting Code rule 8.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of legitimate expectation of privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Legitimate expectations of privacy will vary according to the place and nature of the information, activity or circumstances in question, the extent to which it is in the public domain, if at all, and whether the individual concerned is already in the public eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be circumstances where people can reasonably expect privacy even in a public place; some activities may be so private that filming/recording even in public could infringe privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance public interest and individual privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC must balance the public interest in freedom of expression with the legitimate expectation of privacy by individuals, taking into account ethical, regulatory and legal obligations. Any infringement of privacy in the gathering of material must be proportionate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply proportionality and consider ethical, regulatory and legal obligations (see Section 1 The BBC's Editorial Standards: 1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrusion requires public interest justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any infringement of an individual's privacy without their consent must be justified by demonstrating that the intrusion is outweighed by the public interest. The greater the intrusion, the greater the public interest required to justify it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess level of intrusion and require commensurate weight of public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting private behaviour of public figures — limited grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Content producers should normally only report the private behaviour of public figures where their conduct is unlawful, anti-social or where broader public issues are raised either by the behaviour itself, or by the consequences of it becoming widely known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact of publication by other media may not justify the BBC reporting of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: No 'fishing expeditions' with secret recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Content producers must not go on 'fishing expeditions', i.e. secret recording in search of crime or anti-social behaviour by identifiable individuals, or groups, when there is no prima facie evidence of such behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secret recording should not be used merely to search for wrongdoing without initial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance reporting of human suffering with dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: The public interest in the full and accurate reporting of stories involving human suffering and distress must be balanced with an individual's privacy and respect for their human dignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the need for accurate reporting against harm to dignity and privacy of those affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and lawful handling when gathering personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: When gathering personal information from contributors, audiences and other members of the public, it must be clear how it is intended to be used. It must be handled in accordance with the BBC's Editorial Guidelines and the Data Protection Act 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow relevant Editorial Guidelines and data protection law; see 7.4.58-7.4.63 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: illegal overseas material-gathering
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to gather material illegally outside the UK by disregarding privacy or other similar laws in the relevant country must be referred to Director Editorial Policy and Standards. Programme Legal Advice must also be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop and refer; see 7.4.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: employing/ paying people with criminal records for investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Director Editorial Policy and Standards must approve any proposal to employ and/or pay someone known to have a criminal record or background of illegal activity to work on a BBC investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Director Editorial Policy and Standards prior to approval; see 7.4.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: use of secret recordings made by others
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to use secret recordings made by others must be referred to Editorial Policy prior to approval by a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, by the commissioning editor. If the BBC would not have considered it justifiable to gather the material under similar circumstances, the proposal must be referred to Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral required before approval; see 7.4.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: broadcast of recordings originally made for note-taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to broadcast, without consent, recordings originally made for note-taking purposes must be agreed by Director Editorial Policy and Standards. Permission to broadcast material gathered in this way will only be granted in exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptional circumstances only; see 7.4.31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: equipping third parties with body-worn cameras/mics
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to equip third parties with body-worn cameras and microphones, where to do so might infringe the privacy of an individual or where the third party is entering private premises without permission, must be referred in advance to Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer in advance; see 7.4.32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: unmonitored recording on private property
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal for unmonitored recording equipment on private property without consent of the occupier must be referred to Programme Legal Advice and Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer before proceeding; see 7.4.34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: use of tracking devices that would infringe privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to use a tracking device where it would infringe the privacy of an individual must be referred to Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer prior to authorisation; see 7.4.35.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: private investigator breaching guidelines or breaking law
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal for a private investigator acting for the BBC to breach the Editorial Guidelines or, exceptionally, to break the law in pursuit of an investigation must be approved in advance by a senior editorial figure, who must consult Director Editorial Policy and Standards prior to approval, and Programme Legal Advice must also be consulted where it is believed laws may be broken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict approval and consultation required; see 7.4.42.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: suspicion that BBC staff may break the law during production
rubrics_metrics.description: If during the course of making programmes or content, it is believed laws may be broken by someone working for the BBC, it must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor, who should consult Programme Legal Advice and Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer promptly; see 7.4.13 and 7.4.43.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: proposals to engage in or commission hacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to engage in hacking or commission hacking activities by third parties must be referred in advance to Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer before any hacking activity is authorised; see 7.4.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: secretly recording a doorstep
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to secretly record a doorstep must be agreed with Director Editorial Policy and Standards. Permission to gather material in this way will only be granted in very exceptional circumstances and must be in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very exceptional circumstances and public interest test apply; see 7.4.49.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: secret recording (other than note-taking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to carry out secret recording, other than for note-taking purposes, must be referred to Editorial Policy prior to approval by the relevant senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, by the commissioning editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Policy should consider justification prior to approval; see 7.4.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: deception beyond concealing recording equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deception required to obtain secretly recorded material, beyond the concealing of recording equipment, should be the minimum necessary and proportionate to the subject matter and must be referred to Editorial Policy prior to approval by the relevant senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deception must be proportionate and minimised; refer to Editorial Policy; see 7.4.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: sending someone undercover on an investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to send someone to work undercover on an investigation must be referred to Editorial Policy and Programme Legal Advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer for Editorial Policy and legal consultation; see 7.4.17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: Editorial Policy consultation on job applications by undercover operatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Policy must be consulted about job applications by undercover operatives working on BBC investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Editorial Policy as part of vetting and approval; see 7.4.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: high-risk investigations (serious/violent crime, extremism, terror)
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC Safety's High Risk Team, Editorial Policy and Programme Legal Advice must be consulted before investigating, contacting or potentially secretly recording groups or individuals suspected of being involved in serious or potentially violent criminality, acts of extremism or terror related activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-team consultation required for high-risk subjects; see 7.4.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: identification of secretly recorded research participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to identify individuals or organisations secretly recorded for consumer, scientific or social research without their consent must be referred to Editorial Policy who will consider the public interest in identification and the BBC's fairness obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral required to weigh public interest and fairness; see 7.4.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: featuring identifiable people live without their knowledge (comedy/entertainment/satire)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to feature identifiable people in a live broadcast for comedy, entertainment or satire, without their knowledge, whether in person, on the phone, or via any other medium must be referred to Editorial Policy at the outset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer at the planning stage; see 7.4.28.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: drone use where privacy might be infringed
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to gather material using a drone where it might infringe privacy must be referred to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, the commissioning editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer before approving drone deployments; see 7.4.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: live streaming without alerting those who may be shown
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to transmit a live stream without alerting those who may be shown in the broadcast must be referred to Editorial Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer because lack of notice may infringe privacy; see 7.4.40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: use of private investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to use a private investigator must be approved by a senior editorial figure who may consult Director Editorial Policy and Standards before going ahead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior editorial approval required; see 7.4.42.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: accessing or using data from hacks or leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to access data derived from hacks or leaks must be referred to Editorial Policy and Programme Legal Advice. Where such data has been sent to the BBC, it must be referred to Editorial Policy and Programme Legal Advice before use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer prior to use; legal and editorial review required; see 7.4.44.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: doorstepping after prior interview/statement request
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to doorstep an individual or organisation, where a request has previously been made for an interview or a statement, must be referred to Editorial Policy before approval by a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, by the commissioning editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer when prior request has been made; see 7.4.47.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: doorstepping without prior interview/statement request
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to doorstep an individual or organisation, where an interview or statement has not previously been requested, must be referred to Editorial Policy prior to approval by a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies to the commissioning editor, and a written record of the decision kept. This does not apply to the legitimate gathering of material for the daily news agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer and record decision; daily news gathering is excepted; see 7.4.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: doorstepping for comedy, entertainment or satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to doorstep an individual or organisation for comedy, entertainment or satirical purposes should normally be approved in advance by a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, by the commissioning editor. Editorial Policy should also be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal advance approval plus Editorial Policy consultation; see 7.4.50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: reconstructions/dramatisations involving victims' objections
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision to proceed with a reconstruction or dramatisation of past events involving suffering or trauma, when there are reasonable objections from surviving victims and relatives who have a legitimate expectation of privacy, should be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor, who should normally consult Editorial Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer when victims/relatives object on privacy grounds; consult Editorial Policy; see 7.4.57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: requests from public authorities for contributors' personal information / sharing for safeguarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request by a public authority for a contributor's personal information, or where content producers are proposing to share that information for safeguarding or welfare reasons, must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor, who must refer to Editorial Policy and Programme Legal Advice before information is shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer and consult Editorial Policy and legal advice prior to disclosure; see 7.4.61.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: collecting personal information on BBC Public Service sites that may be disclosed to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to collect personal information on a BBC Public Service website which might be disclosed to third parties, including BBC Commercial Services, must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor, who may wish to consult Information Rights and BBC Fair Trading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer and consider Information Rights and Fair Trading implications; see 7.4.62.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: revealing under-18's personal details to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to reveal an under-18's personal details to a third party without their consent must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor, who should consult Editorial Policy, Safeguarding, and Information Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer and consult safeguarding and information-rights teams before disclosure; see 7.4.63.
